designStatus: Original parameterised framework task designs, not learner observations, validated measures or a nationally selected language pair.

requiredBeforeUse: Actual role language and script, separately labelled evidence for each role.
Qualified speaker/script user, expert-checked materials, appropriate response criteria.
Access, familiarity and assistance distinguished from independent performance.
Retain actual source progression and the precise very-unfamiliar-R2 emergence/early-Preparatory consolidation exception where it applies.
notInferred: A fixed pair is required before framework curation.
Conditional graph candidates are safe unconditional links.
A Full authoring label is a learner mastery result.

protocols.task: In the relevant role language, hold an unscripted familiar planning exchange, then describe a real experience to a listener who was not there. Change the setting or audience for a second exchange.
evidenceDesign: Listen and respond to the partner across several connected turns, maintain relevant detail and repair misunderstanding.
Distinguish persistently blocked meaning or entirely rehearsed turns from connected responsive communication; do not impose native speed or accent.
Declare familiarity/support separately in R1 and R2; retain early-Preparatory consolidation where the source unfamiliar-R2 exception applies.
nearMisses: A memorised speech offered as conversational fluency.
R1 success treated as evidence of R2 word knowledge.
protocols.transfer: Change topic and partner without supplying the responses.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The whole discussion and description claims include turn-taking, topic continuity, audible intelligible detail and logical organisation; these are independently checked.

protocols.task: Read a short actual-role text aloud without showing it, then ask for a concise account of its main ideas. Contrast an accurate short summary with an accurate but unselective retelling. Add a short audio/video and a simple chart case for the complete existing summary candidate.
evidenceDesign: Select central ideas, preserve meaning and omit nonessential detail without merely repeating lines.
Distinguish summarising from paraphrasing every detail; ask for a reason one detail can be omitted.
Check different media and a supplied simple quantitative display when assessing the full existing candidate.
nearMisses: Adult supplies the important ideas before the response.
Reading/writing or English print conventions silently required for a purely heard-text source task.
protocols.transfer: Use a new passage with a different structure and mix of important/minor details.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: A4→-Du→sMA→ZhUu→XeM→1KC reaches left-to-right print through a written note-taking path. The intrinsic operation fits but remains a conditional graph candidate; no link or dependency change is authored.

protocols.task: Prepare a short topic report, a welcome or small-event introduction, and a brief reasoned class contribution. Include collaborative discussion so prepared presentation does not replace responding to others.
evidenceDesign: Organise relevant facts or ideas with a clear sequence, understandable pace and sufficient detail.
State a view with a reason, listen to a different view and respond to its actual content.
Record/rehearse one talk and make a meaningful clarity or organisation improvement.
nearMisses: Reciting a memorised text without adapting its purpose or responding to a listener.
Requiring Standard English, adult debate procedure or an advanced persuasive-writing bundle.
protocols.transfer: Change purpose from informing peers to introducing an event, then change audience or topic.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Reporting/recounting includes factual organisation and a personal-event account; Expressing & Justifying Opinions includes reasoned answers and participation in presentations, performance, role play and debate. Each direct shared operation has a complete primary stage-end task, without the older Formal Debates claim.

protocols.task: Use unfamiliar-to-task prose, a short poem and an informational description in the actual role language. Pause for a prediction, ask for an inference from evidence, and invite a mental picture that changes after new information.
evidenceDesign: Explain a prediction from textual clues and revise it when evidence changes.
Distinguish stated information from inferred meaning and justify the inference.
Sketch/describe an imagined scene or process, then compare it with an illustration or other version and revise its meaning.
nearMisses: Any plausible guess accepted without evidence.
A picture copied without constructing or revising meaning from words.
protocols.transfer: Change text form and subject while retaining accessible language.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Prediction includes titles/events; inference includes story characters and factual details; visualisation includes listening, viewing and reading, with revision and inferred meaning. Suitable additional cases cover the whole existing claims rather than a single story illustration.

protocols.task: Independently read a short informational text and a narrative. Identify central information, connected details and an evidenced conclusion or message.
evidenceDesign: Explain why a supporting detail matters to the main meaning.
Use actions/events or linked facts to draw a conclusion, allowing different defensible interpretations.
Keep heard-text comprehension separate from independent reading.
nearMisses: Listing every fact with no selection or connection.
Inventing a message contradicted by the text.
protocols.transfer: Read a second text with different relevant/irrelevant details and a different conclusion.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Main-topic, inference and sequence/message claims supply the source operation without requiring the wider written-note-taking bundle. Their complete narrative and informational checks are included.

protocols.task: Plan and write a short actual-role piece with a clear beginning and ending, sequenced ideas, paragraph groups and purposeful headings. Present an alternative grouping and ask why one serves the reader better.
evidenceDesign: Choose an order and boundaries based on meaning rather than page length.
Keep a visible plan, compose the piece and revise at least one grouping/heading choice.
Use actual target-language labels or plain explanation rather than require English terminology.
nearMisses: Only copying supplied headings or paragraph breaks.
Declaring all writing-process vocabulary mastered from one organised piece.
protocols.transfer: Organise a second piece with a different purpose and a different point where the topic changes.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The unchanged AvJ paragraph operation plus a complete authored piece and independent boundary repair accounts for the source organising strategies after separate reviewed prerequisite corrections. The broader 9P pre-writing operation is not necessary to this source requirement and is not published as an additional claim contribution.

protocols.task: Write a focused actual-role paragraph about an experience or a topic understood from a text, then organise a second short informational piece under suitable topic groups.
evidenceDesign: Related sentences develop a focus rather than merely repeat one fact.
Explain/revise a paragraph boundary and use a heading where it helps.
Distinguish the child’s understanding from verbatim copying or adult dictation.
nearMisses: Three unrelated sentences accepted merely because they are written in one block.
Adult-created boundaries counted as independent organisation.
protocols.transfer: Explain another unfamiliar but accessible topic in a fresh paragraph.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The whole paragraph claim retains focused grouping, suitable narrative/non-narrative task cases, boundary explanation and purposeful headings. Its three broader prerequisite bundles are now soft support after independent within-English witnesses; no source requirement or claim field is removed.

protocols.task: Across a small integrated portfolio, make a poster or invitation, an original short poem, and a story containing a plausible exchange between characters. Use the actual role language and reader-appropriate script conventions.
evidenceDesign: Give a poster/invitation the information its reader needs and explain one layout/wording choice.
Compose a new poetic line/pattern; written composition and expressive recitation remain separate checks.
Develop people, place and an ordered event/problem with meaningful dialogue rather than only label speakers.
nearMisses: Copying an adult-completed text or changing only a supplied name.
One poem offered as evidence of all poster/narrative/dialogue requirements.
protocols.transfer: Change audience/purpose and create a second text with appropriately different choices.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: YNe is a direct shared composition component, with its whole written, sound-pattern and memorised-recitation checks retained. AHX/vau have direct intrinsic fits but unchanged conditional inherited writing gates. Source task design covers the other forms without pretending those unsafe links are published.

protocols.task: Before use, a competent speaker/script user specifies suitable actual-language sentence/grammar/text-structure criteria and checks the task/model. Ask the learner to express relationships and revise a meaning-changing construction in a familiar text.
evidenceDesign: Judge intelligibility, grammatical relationships and intended meaning using actual language conventions.
For complex-structure oral goals, include a connected relation between ideas rather than only disconnected short labels.
Do not assume English SVO, articles, adjective order, tense morphology, capitals or punctuation are universal.
nearMisses: Testing English grammar knowledge as universal R1/R2 structure.
Approving a translation without checking whether its constructions have the same function.
protocols.transfer: Express the same relationship in another locally appropriate form or change audience/purpose.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: No unqualified English grammar claim is substituted. The source remains a formal role-bound requirement; material/assessor binding is needed at use, not a nationwide fixed language pair.

protocols.task: Use actual-role home/school and subject-area texts or talk containing familiar and unfamiliar words. Discuss a reasoned meaning from context, connect it to known vocabulary, and apply the word in a new exchange or written sentence.
evidenceDesign: Infer tentatively from context and verify/refine when additional information appears.
Choose accurate words for subject meaning, explain a technical term and use it appropriately.
Include functional need/choice/help/response exchanges as well as new-word examples; no universal vocabulary count.
nearMisses: A copied definition without appropriate contextual use.
An English equivalent automatically counted as R1 or R2 knowledge.
protocols.transfer: Use a different subject text and a new home/school situation.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete generic vocabulary claims include discussing meanings, contextual inference and oral/written application. Wz includes academic and domain terms across several subjects. R1 C-4.1 and C-4.2 remain distinct printed positions, not duplicate mastery topics.

protocols.task: Provide genuinely accessible actual-role books, a real borrowing or equivalent accessible library-loan route, time to read at home, and repeated opportunities to choose or revisit a text. Record access constraints and child choices without prescribing enthusiasm.
evidenceDesign: For the R1 borrowing position, design an actual repeated loan/home-reading opportunity rather than only show a library picture.
Separate access, unfamiliar language or inaccessible text from engagement; retain availability constraints explicitly.
Allow changed preference or declining a book without a negative mastery label.
nearMisses: An arbitrary book quota or compulsory positive feeling.
Accurate oral reading or a recommendation substituted for access and voluntary engagement.
protocols.transfer: Offer another varied collection and repeat the opportunity in a changed context.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: These are formal contextual participation/engagement requirements. No new mastery claim, compulsory reading score or learner field is introduced; lack of a local library resource is not silently relabelled learner failure.

protocols.task: Build a role-labelled oral portfolio combining connected conversation, heard meaning, a concise summary where required, an organised presentation and collaborative discussion.
evidenceDesign: Assess each actual source requirement rather than count linked topics.
Retain R1 language-structure conditions and the conditional R1 heard-summary candidate; do not transfer R1 attainment to R2.
Use integrated tasks but keep the evidence attributable to each operation and declared support.
nearMisses: Prepared presentation used to certify all spontaneous interaction.
Source goals declared complete graph mastery despite conditional components.
protocols.transfer: Change familiar purpose, text form and audience.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The relevant component protocols apply. R1 and R2 share some operations but retain their distinct source expectations and progression.

protocols.task: Use independently read actual-role narrative, poetry and informational/functional materials, combining the appropriate meaning, strategy, fluency and print-convention tasks.
evidenceDesign: For R1, include unfamiliar-to-task texts and varied comprehension strategies.
For R2, retain script/print binding, the conditional fluency graph case and a separate contextual reading-choice opportunity.
Distinguish source-fit task authoring from actual learner reading attainment.

For the R1 text-form component, distinguish a story, poem and non-fiction text, and identify the author/illustrator and their roles in a suitable illustrated book. These account for the complete existing text-types claim without pretending every source reading task must itself have an illustrator.
nearMisses: Counting comprehension links as a complete script/fluency profile.
An adult read-aloud substituted for every independent-reading task.
protocols.transfer: Use a new collection with different layout and purpose, within declared language accessibility.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete contributing shared claims retain their extra informational, sensory and inference cases. Conditional print/fluency requirements are not silently dropped.

protocols.task: Create a small actual-role portfolio spanning clear information/experience writing, purposeful poster/invitation, original poem and narrative/dialogue. Use planning, revision and target-language structure checks.
evidenceDesign: Account for information, ideas, experiences and appropriate emotional expression without forcing personal disclosure.
Keep purpose, audience, sequence and coherence visible in the actual written work.
Retain conditional grammar and inherited-gate cases instead of claiming all graph requirements are directly representable.
nearMisses: A single memorised poem offered as full writing-goal coverage.
R1 writing credited to R2 or English writing vocabulary presumed universal.
protocols.transfer: Change purpose and topic, then explain/revise a meaningful decision in a fresh piece.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Each named writing protocol retains the full intrinsic candidate operations; conditional candidates are not published as unconditional associations.

protocols.task: Hear a short poem, story and familiar conversation in R2. Explain a central idea, distinguish it from a minor detail, and respond relevantly to the actual exchange.
evidenceDesign: Use evidence from words/events rather than a supplied answer picture.
Include a conversational response or paraphrase, not only narrative character naming.
Declare prompts and unfamiliar vocabulary without treating supported emergence as independent fluency.
nearMisses: Guessing from pictures while not understanding the spoken text.
Requiring written notes or English print knowledge for the heard-text task.
protocols.transfer: Change text genre and conversation purpose.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete literary/informational listening, sequence/message and responsive-listening claims are included through suitable additional cases; no fixed English inventory is a hard prerequisite.

protocols.task: Hear an unfamiliar R2 narrative, then identify people, connected events and an evidenced central meaning. Add a short informational passage for the full sequence/message claim.
evidenceDesign: Retell important events in a meaningful order.
Explain a message from an event rather than repeat an adult-provided moral.
Distinguish heard narrative from independent decoding.
nearMisses: Only naming pictures or reproducing one memorised sentence.
protocols.transfer: Use another story with a different resolution and a different informational connection.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Complete story-element, narrative-message and informational-connection checks remain intact; R1 success is not transferred.

protocols.task: Use familiar actual-R2 words for expert-checked spoken syllable counting, joining and separation, then mark pronunciation divisions beside a familiar written word as a reading aid.
evidenceDesign: Keep the oral unit distinct from letters, written akshar boundaries and arbitrary English conventions.
Vary word length and supplied unit sequences, avoiding an answer picture.
Do not test an untaught foreign vocabulary word while labelling the failure phonological.
nearMisses: Counting letters or reproducing a memorised clap pattern instead of analysing speech.
protocols.transfer: Use another familiar word with a different syllable pattern.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The full Syllables claim includes counting and written-word pronunciation support as well as the source joining/separation operation; no English phoneme inventory is imposed.

protocols.task: Use actual-R2 books and short texts with expert-checked layout, word/sentence segmentation and punctuation conventions. Ask the learner to show the reading path and interpret a meaningful boundary or punctuation cue.
evidenceDesign: Specify actual script, forms and accepted response before use.
Include structure, words/sentences and a contextual punctuation example rather than only recognise the title.
Retain differences between speech units, written symbols and layout.
nearMisses: Imposing Latin capitals or a universal left-to-right path.
protocols.transfer: Use a different layout within the same actual script.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: No universal English print-convention link is published; source status remains formal and the script-binding condition remains explicit.

protocols.task: Use independently read R2 passages with locally specified scoring units, accurate accepted readings, appropriate pacing and meaningful pauses. Include rereading/self-correction and a separate meaning check.
evidenceDesign: Distinguish accuracy, expression and understanding in the actual language.
Record support and use a new matched passage rather than only a fully rehearsed performance.
Keep the existing basic-reading whole-claim check separate from any English inventory assumption.
nearMisses: English GPC/LTR knowledge used as a universal entry gate.
A memorised passage alone accepted as independent reading.
protocols.transfer: Read a different familiar-topic passage with different phrasing/mood.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: V-L→Zhvw reaches English-specific hard requirements. The intrinsic task design is accounted, but the association remains report-only until a separate reviewed graph decision.

protocols.task: Independently read R2 story, poem and picture/text story-poster material, explaining meaningful events, wording and intended purpose. Include a short factual connection for the whole sequence/message claim.
evidenceDesign: Support an interpretation with a specific verbal or visual detail.
Explain how picture and words contribute rather than infer all meaning from an unrelated image.
Distinguish a poem’s wording effect from a forced positive feeling.
nearMisses: Recognising a genre name while not comprehending the text.
protocols.transfer: Read a new combined picture/text example with a different message.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Sequence/message, expressive language and text-purpose claims retain their full narrative/nonfiction, recurring/sensory and contrasting-purpose cases, including genre/author/illustrator prerequisite tasks.

protocols.task: Write an actual-R2 poster, invitation and simple safe instruction text for a declared reader. Choose information, words and layout to serve that purpose, then revise after a reader response.
evidenceDesign: Include the information a reader needs to act without adult filling-in.
Explain one meaningful wording/layout change.
When assessing the complete multimodal candidate, include the paragraph/diagram/caption and a supplied digital or print-tool case appropriate to its actual whole requirements.
nearMisses: Copying an adult-written invitation without selecting relevant information.
A decorative picture accepted without meaningful actual-R2 writing.
protocols.transfer: Change audience or action and design another functional text.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The intrinsic AHX operation fits, but its inherited paragraph/writing chains remain conditional; no unsafe unqualified association is published.
